newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Afghan Taleban said to take opposition airbase.
newsitem.headline: Afghan Taleban said to take opposition airbase.

text.p: Afghanistan's Islamic Taleban movement on Friday captured the main opposition airbase of Bagram, north of the capital Kabul, a Pakistan-based Afghan news service said.
The Afghan Islamic press (AIP) said the Taleban forces entered Bagram on Friday evening after capturing the nearby opposition stronghold of Qarabagh.
There was no immediate independent confirmation of this report or of a major Taleban offensive after a lull of several weeks in fighting north of Kabul.
The Taleban captured the Afghan capital in late September when it ousted the government of President Burhanuddin Rabbani.

Official Kabul radio, monitored in the Pakistani capital Islamabad, earlier said the Taleban militia seized Qarabagh district from the forces of the northern alliance of the ousted government Uzbek chief General Abdul Rashid Dostum after a day-long offensive.
AIP said at least 50 opposition fighters were killed and 230 captured in Qarabagh, including Abdus Sabur Farid of the Hezb-i-Islami party who briefly served as prime minister under Rabbani in 1993.

The Taleban had taken Qarabagh and Bagram immediately after capturing Kabul on September 27 but it was forced to withdraw after forces led by Rabbani's top military commander, Ahmad Shah Masood, counter-attacked.
Bagram was used by Soviet occupying forces as the main airbase to fight mujahideen guerrillas in the 1980s and was later used by Rabbani's government to fight its opponents.
But it became unusable for aircraft during fighting there between the Taleban and Masood's forces after the September 27 takeover of Kabul.
Masood's forces shot down a Taleban helicopter near Bagram on Friday, AIP said, quoting Taleban sources.
The helicopter had two pilots aboard and there was no information about their fate, it said.
